thread:
kevin: quick heads-up 1 I'm opening a tiny PR to clarify Private installer preflight for on-prem HSMs. Saw multiple tickets where gateway SNAT hides caller IP and auditors complain. Need a short review.

ana: can you paste the exact firewall snippets you plan to add? infra likes both iptables and nft variants.

kevin: pasted in PR comment 1 iptables (insert RETURN before MASQUERADE): ```sh
# exempt HSM subnet from MASQUERADE so source IP is preserved
iptables -t nat -I POSTROUTING 1 -s 10.240.0.0/16 -d 172.18.200.0/24 -j RETURN
iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -o eth0 -m comment --comment "egress-masq" -j MASQUERADE
``` nftables version (accept before masquerade): ```nft
table ip nat {
  chain postrouting {
    type nat hook postrouting priority 100;
    ip saddr 10.240.0.0/16 ip daddr 172.18.200.0/24 accept
    oifname "eth0" masquerade comment "egress-masq"
  }
}
```

sam: nit 1 show the order explicitly in the examples and mention that RETURN vs ACCEPT ordering matters (iptables vs nft). Also add a short preflight checklist: ip_forward, route to HSM, nft/iptables rule checks, and clock sync.

kevin: added preflight snippet to the PR: ```sh
# preflight checks
sysctl -n net.ipv4.ip_forward || echo "ERROR: ip_forward disabled"
ip route get 172.18.200.10 || echo "WARN: no route to HSM"
# quick NAT rule checks
iptables -t nat -S | grep -E "MASQUERADE|RETURN" || true
nft list ruleset | grep -E "masquerade|postrouting" || true
# clock sync (HSM certs are strict)
date -u && timedatectl show -p NTPSynchronized || echo "WARN: clock unsynchronized"
```

ana: for sealed / air-gapped installs mention chrony pointing to a local NTP appliance (do not use public pool defaults). Can you add a tiny chrony snippet and a one-line caveat about not leaking external NTP traffic?

kevin: added chrony example and note: ```ini
# /etc/chrony.conf - point to local NTP appliance
server ntp.internal.local iburst
# avoid public pools in sealed installs
pool 0.pool.ntp.org iburst offline
```

sam: nice. Ops teams also like concrete client examples. Add a Go snippet showing TLS client certs to KMS and a short Rust example for teams using Rust infra. Keep them minimal.

kevin: added both to PR comments. Go example: ```go
c, _ := redwood.NewPrivateClient(redwood.ClientOptions{
  KMSEndpoint: "https://kms.internal:8443",
  ClientCert:  "/etc/ssl/client.crt",
  ClientKey:   "/etc/ssl/client.key",
  CACert:      "/etc/ssl/ca.crt",
})
_ = c.Healthcheck()
``` Rust example: ```rust
let client = redwood::private::Client::new(&redwood::Config {
  kms_endpoint: "https://kms.internal:8443".into(),
  client_cert: Some(("/etc/ssl/client.crt".into(), "/etc/ssl/client.key".into())),
  ca_cert: Some("/etc/ssl/ca.crt".into()),
  ..Default::default()
});
client.healthcheck().await?;
```

ana: small editorial 1 rename "preserve src" to "preserve source IP for HSM audit logs" per compliance. Also the HSM plugin link in the docs is stale; link-bot should suggest the canonical integrations path.

link-bot: automated suggestion: replace "/hsm-plugin/" with "/integrations/hsm/pkcs11/" in PR #2411.

sam: one more request 1 add a tiny netns test script so engineers can validate locally (bridged namespace and curl with client cert). Low friction keeps support tickets down.

kevin: included test-hsm-netns.sh in PR: ```sh
# local test harness: create namespace and veth pair to simulate gateway
sudo ip netns add hsmtest
sudo ip link add veth-host type veth peer name veth-ns
sudo ip link set veth-ns netns hsmtest
sudo ip addr add 10.240.0.1/24 dev veth-host
sudo ip netns exec hsmtest ip addr add 10.240.0.2/24 dev veth-ns
sudo ip netns exec hsmtest ip route add default via 10.240.0.1
# from namespace test a host-local HSM emulator
sudo ip netns exec hsmtest curl -v https://172.18.200.10:8443/health --resolve "172.18.200.10:8443:172.18.200.10" --cert client.crt --key client.key
```

ana: love the script. One tiny addition 1 include an ASCII packet-flow diagram in the docs (3 lines) to help people orient quickly.

kevin: added a compact diagram and linked an issue to add a proper SVG in the next docs sprint. Diagram in PR: 

Host 10.240.0.2 --(via gateway, no masq)-> 172.18.200.10 HSM
           gateway: MASQ for other egress but ACCEPT/RETURN for 172.18.200.0/24
